clue.text: Spare man of Italian origin full of taste

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase standing for a strongly flavoured cheese

indicators.note: the phrase asks for the two words to be recast into an Italian-born form, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An Italian-born bachelor with a refined palate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spare man' looks like a bachelor; rearranged it spells the hard cheese from Parma, which is full of flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard cheese from Parma is prized for its strong, savoury flavour.

clue.text: One making an early start in this colour may well succeed

definitions.text: One making an early start in this colour may well succeed

parts.words: One making an early start in this colour may well succeed
parts.note: a baby 'born in' this royal colour is heir to a throne and may succeed to it

explanation.walkthrough: To be 'born in the' colour is to be born into royalty; 'succeed' means inherit the crown, not do well.
explanation.definitionFit: The imperial colour, as in the idiom for royal birth.

clue.text: About little Christina, she's an eyeful!

parts.note: re means about, concerning
Tina is a short form of the name Christina

explanation.surface: Admiring talk about a pretty girl called Christina.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an eyeful' means a looker, but the definition is literal: something that fills part of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye, so literally part of an eyeful.

clue.text: Arouse a townsman in the river

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the townsman goes within the river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
cit is an old short form of citizen, a townsman

explanation.surface: Stirring up a citizen who has fallen into the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe is a river in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up or stimulate.

clue.text: Like that broken engagement feeling ?

parts.note: when an engagement is broken off it is 'all over', and one feels vaguely unwell

explanation.walkthrough: The word means vaguely unwell throughout the body; the clue reads it as the feeling that it is all over.
explanation.definitionFit: Vaguely unwell, with a general sense of malaise.

clue.text: Look out, man, look out!

parts.note: to look out is to gaze
bo is an old American form of address for a fellow, a man

explanation.surface: Someone shouting a warning to a friend twice.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the second 'look out', read as a noun: a garden summerhouse built for the view.
explanation.definitionFit: A summerhouse or belvedere is a structure built to give a view, a lookout point.

clue.text: Describing the proverbial horse, up to the water's edge at least

definitions.text: Describing the proverbial horse, up to the water's edge at least

parts.words: Describing the proverbial horse, up to the water's edge at least
parts.note: you can lead a horse to water but cannot make it drink, so it is willing only that far

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says a horse can be led to water but not made to drink, so it is compliant only as far as the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Willing to be led or persuaded, responsive.

clue.text: Net value emerging finally

definitions.note: an adverb standing for an adjective meaning coming at last

indicators.note: the letters come out in a new order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An accountant's net figure that turns up at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'emerging' rearranges NET VALUE. The answer is an adjective; 'finally' stands for 'coming finally'.
explanation.definitionFit: Happening at the end of a process, ultimately resulting.

clue.text: Covers for love-songs about spring

indicators.note: about means going round, so love and songs surround spring

parts.note: O is love, a zero score in tennis
lays are ballads or songs
ver is Latin for spring

explanation.surface: Sleeves for records of romantic songs about springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated 'love-songs' must be split into two pieces, and 'about' wraps them around the Latin word for spring.
explanation.definitionFit: Layers spread over something to cover it.

clue.text: Bag for a broadcaster !

parts.note: a broadcaster is read as a sower scattering seed, who might carry a small netted bag

explanation.surface: A satchel for someone who works on radio.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'broadcaster' originally scattered seed by hand; the answer is a small netted handbag, from Latin for net.
explanation.definitionFit: A small drawstring handbag carried by women, originally of netting.

clue.text: Unruffled titular adjunct

definitions.meaning: a word added to a title

explanation.definitionFit: Means calm and placid, and is also the honorific word attached to certain royal titles.

clue.text: Upset, I've let in a soothing agent

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone distressed after admitting a calming remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' rearranges the letters of I'VE LET IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A medicine or ointment that relieves pain or irritation, a palliative.

clue.text: Stick at fifty for this picture ?

parts.note: to stick is to paste
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Hanging a picture when you are fifty years old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawing made with chalky crayons in soft colours.

clue.text: Where a stuck-up lot get booked ?

definitions.text: Where a stuck-up lot get booked ?

parts.words: Where a stuck-up lot get booked
parts.note: a collection of gummed things stuck up on pages in a book

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuck-up' means snobbish, but here it is a set of gummed items mounted in a volume.
explanation.definitionFit: A book in which a philatelist mounts a collection.

clue.text: Lily in purple is flighty!

definitions.meaning: a plant of the lily family whose snake's-head species has chequered purple flowers
a butterfly, a creature given to flight

explanation.definitionFit: Both a lily-family plant with purple chequered bells and a family of orange-brown butterflies.

clue.text: Hesitations displayed by lightweights

definitions.meaning: qualms that make one hold back
an apothecaries' weight of twenty grains, a very small measure

explanation.definitionFit: Moral qualms, and also small apothecaries' weights of twenty grains each.

clue.text: Practise victimisation ?

parts.note: read literally as making a victim, offering one up in sacrifice

explanation.walkthrough: 'Victimisation' suggests bullying, but literally it means making a sacrificial victim, by burning.
explanation.definitionFit: To sacrifice, especially by fire.

clue.text: Decidedly pointed heading to some columns !

definitions.text: Decidedly pointed heading to some columns !

parts.words: Decidedly pointed heading to some columns
parts.note: the triangular top over a classical portico, read as a sharp headline over newspaper columns

explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading' and 'columns' suggest a newspaper, but the columns are architectural.
explanation.definitionFit: The triangular gable topping a classical building's row of columns.

clue.text: How does it come about some browns are unwieldy ?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word goes around the second

parts.note: taken as written
umbers are brown earth pigments

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about why brown things are hard to handle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How does it come about' reads as a question; in fact 'come' is placed 'about' UMBERS, and 'How does it' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Bulky and awkward to carry or manage.

clue.text: He pronounces the coin an old Greek one

definitions.text: the coin an old Greek one
definitions.meaning: an ancient Greek coin of gold or silver

explanation.definitionFit: Literally one who declares, and also an ancient Greek coin.

clue.text: Point to a belief in manuscript effusion

parts.note: S, south, is a compass point
a creed is a set of beliefs

explanation.surface: Pointing to someone's faith in a long handwritten outpouring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' and 'in' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, tedious piece of writing.

clue.text: Feel very upset about Pussyfoot ? Fine !

definitions.note: an exclamation meaning all is in good order, as in the phrase 'in fine' condition

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the scrambled letters go around the teetotal one
very upset means thrown into disorder, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: 'Pussyfoot' Johnson was an American campaigner against alcohol, so he stands for TT, teetotal

explanation.surface: Someone distressed about a cautious friend, then deciding it is all right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very upset' scrambles the first word and 'about' wraps it round the abstainer; William 'Pussyfoot' Johnson was an American campaigner for prohibition.
explanation.definitionFit: Good condition or trim, usually heard in the idiom of being in fine shape.

clue.text: Moreland ?

parts.note: read as the land of Thomas More, the imaginary island of his 1516 book

explanation.walkthrough: Sir Thomas More wrote of an ideal commonwealth on an imaginary island; his 'land' is that place.
explanation.definitionFit: An imagined perfect society, named from Thomas More's book.

clue.text: A little bit of grammar

definitions.meaning: a minor indeclinable part of speech, such as an adverb or conjunction

explanation.definitionFit: Means a minute fragment, and in grammar a small function word.

clue.text: Browning's was lost for a handful of silver

definitions.text: Browning's was lost for a handful of silver

parts.words: Browning's was lost for a handful of silver
parts.note: Robert Browning's poem 'The Lost ...' begins 'Just for a handful of silver he left us'

explanation.walkthrough: Browning's poem accused Wordsworth of deserting the radical cause; its title names the deserter as the lost one at the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A chief or head of a movement, the figure of Browning's poem title.

clue.text: Aid with this for the criminal classes?

definitions.text: Aid with this for the criminal classes?

parts.words: Aid with this for the criminal classes
parts.note: the legal term for helping someone commit a crime

explanation.walkthrough: Aiding a criminal is 'aiding and' this legal act.
explanation.definitionFit: Encouraging or helping in wrongdoing, as in the legal phrase 'aiding and' it.

clue.text: Old faders-away ?

parts.note: the song says old soldiers never die, they only fade away; veteran soldiers are called 'old' this

explanation.walkthrough: 'Old sweats' is British slang for veteran soldiers, who in the song 'simply fade away'.
explanation.definitionFit: Veterans, in the phrase old soldiers known as old ones of this kind.

clue.text: The place for radio toxopholites

parts.note: toxophilites are archers, and the radio soap about a farming family named Archer is set in a village

explanation.walkthrough: The Archers is a long-running BBC radio soap about a farming family; its fictional village is the place meant.
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional village where the BBC radio serial The Archers is set.
